statements.text: [[revenue|Revenue]] grew 2.3% in the year ended December 27, 2025, to $93.9 billion. This means the company sold more than the year before.
In the [[quarter|quarter]] ended September 5, 2026, revenue was $25.3 billion, up 5.6% from the same quarter a year earlier.
[[net-income|Net income]], the profit left after all costs and taxes, fell 14% to $8.2 billion in the year ended December 27, 2025.
After paying for the products it sold, the company kept about $54 of every $100 of sales. This is called its [[gross-margin|gross margin]].
Out of every $100 of sales, about $9 was left as profit after all costs and taxes. This is called its [[profit-margin|profit margin]].
Its day-to-day business brought in $12.1 billion of cash in the year ended December 27, 2025. This is called [[cash-from-operations|cash from operations]].
On September 5, 2026, the company had $10.7 billion in [[cash-and-equivalents|cash and cash equivalents]], money it can use quickly.
On September 5, 2026, it owed $42.7 billion in [[long-term-debt|long-term debt and lease obligations due after the next 12 months]].

figures.label: long-term debt and lease obligations due after the next 12 months

statements.text: On that date it owed more in long-term debt than it held in cash.

figures.label: long-term debt and lease obligations due after the next 12 months

statements.text: On September 5, 2026, the company had $32.6 billion in cash and other assets it expects to use within a year, against $34.5 billion of bills due within a year. That is about $0.94 for every $1 it owes soon, less than enough to cover them. This is its [[current-ratio|current ratio]].
It owned $112 billion in [[assets|assets]] and owed $89.5 billion in [[total-liabilities|total liabilities]], so it owned about $1.25 for every $1 it owed.
For every $1 of [[shareholders-equity|shareholders' equity]] ($22.3 billion), it owed about $1.91 in long-term debt ($42.7 billion). This is its [[debt-to-equity|debt-to-equity ratio]].

figures.label: long-term debt and lease obligations due after the next 12 months

statements.text: Its business brought in $12.1 billion of cash in the year ended December 27, 2025 and spent $4.4 billion on [[capital-expenditure|buildings and equipment]], leaving $7.7 billion of [[free-cash-flow|free cash flow]]: money it could use for dividends, buybacks, paying down debt or growing.

figures.label: spending on buildings, equipment and other long-term assets

statements.text: Free cash flow was smaller than its [[net-income|net income]] ($8.2 billion) that year, meaning less of its accounting profit turned into spare cash.

figures.label: spending on buildings, equipment and other long-term assets

statements.text: In the year ended December 27, 2025, the company spent $1 billion buying back its own shares ([[share-buyback|buybacks]]), paid $7.6 billion in [[dividend|dividends]] to shareholders and invested $4.4 billion in buildings and equipment.

figures.label: spending on buildings, equipment and other long-term assets

statements.text: It earned about $43 of profit for every $100 of [[shareholders-equity|shareholders' equity]] in the year ended December 27, 2025. This is its [[return-on-equity|return on equity]] (42.9%).
[[eps|Earnings per share]] (diluted) fell 13.7% to $6.00 in the year ended December 27, 2025.
Over the 5 years to December 27, 2025, its [[operating-margin|operating margin]] fell to 12.2%, from 14%.
In the year to December 2025, it made $93.9 billion in [[revenue|sales]], 2.3% more than the year before. Sales in its latest three months (to September 2026) were up 5.6% on a year earlier.
In the year to December 2025, it kept $8.2 billion as [[net-income|profit]] after paying all its costs and taxes: about $9 of every $100 it made in sales, its [[profit-margin|profit margin]].

On September 5, 2026, for every $1 of bills due within a year, it had about $0.94 in cash and other things it expected to turn into cash in that time: less than it owed soon, so it relied on money still to come in. This is its [[current-ratio|current ratio]].
On September 5, 2026, it owed $42.7 billion in [[long-term-debt|loans and bonds]] not due for repayment within a year and held $10.7 billion in [[cash-and-equivalents|cash]].

statements.text: In the year to December 2025, its everyday business brought in $12.1 billion in [[cash-from-operations|cash]]. After paying for [[capital-expenditure|new buildings and equipment]], $7.7 billion was [[free-cash-flow|left over]].

statements.text: In the year to December 2025, its biggest uses of money were: paying [[dividend|dividends]] to shareholders: $7.6 billion; [[capital-expenditure|new buildings and equipment]]: $4.4 billion; and [[share-buyback|buying back its own shares]]: $1 billion.
